items.stem: Why hold out a separate test set when evaluating a model?

options.text: To estimate performance on data the model has not seen
options.rationale: Correct: a held-out set estimates generalisation.

options.text: To give the model more data to learn from
options.rationale: The test set is not used for training.

options.text: To guarantee the model is unbiased
options.rationale: A test set does not guarantee fairness.
It does not affect training speed meaningfully.

items.explanation: Correct: a held-out set estimates generalisation.

items.stem: Which TWO are forms of data leakage? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Using future information not available at prediction time
options.rationale: Correct: leaking the future inflates performance.

options.text: Fitting a scaler on the full dataset before splitting
options.rationale: Correct: that leaks test statistics into training.
Splitting first is the correct practice.
That is good practice, not leakage.

items.explanation: Correct: leaking the future inflates performance.

items.stem: A p-value of 0.03 most accurately means what?

options.text: If the null hypothesis were true, data this extreme would occur about 3% of the time
options.rationale: Correct: that is the definition of a p-value.

options.text: There is a 97% chance the result is real
options.rationale: A p-value is not the probability the hypothesis is true.
p-values do not measure effect size.

items.explanation: Correct: that is the definition of a p-value.
